_about.what: HAND-AUTHORED, and the only file under docs/ that is. Raven's per-monster part review: the name a parts row carries, the name each dropdown item carries, and which item the row opens on.
_about.written_by: NOTHING. No script writes this file and none ever should. Its four neighbours are all generated and WILL overwrite whatever is put in them -- partnames.json by build-part-names.py, part-rest.json by build-partrest.py, part-states.json by build-partstates.py, monsters.json by harvest-monsters.py. buildlib.write_json_atomic refuses this basename so a future script cannot take it by accident.
_about.meaning: An entry here means one thing: a human looked at this row against the render. That is why it is not seeded from partnames.json -- a seeded name could not be told from a typed one.
_about.rowKeys: monster id -> rows -> the row's part-id set, exactly as clusterGroups() joins it: numeric order, comma, no spaces. The same key partnames.json uses, so the two line up row for row.
_about.optionKeys: an option's ON-set -- the ids printed after 'on' in the label, with the rage ladder's own parts stripped as groupLabelWithout strips them. 'none' for the all-off option. NEVER a group index: those are invisible in the UI, and a ladder choice's rep is just its first member. Verified unique per row across all 540 multi-member rows in the library.
_about.resolution: exact ON-set match first, then a UNIQUE containment fallback. 0 or 2+ matches warns and resolves to nothing. Exact-first is load-bearing: em001_04 row 8,11,12,101 has options 11,101 / 12,101 / 8, so the bare key '101' is ambiguous and must be rejected rather than silently first-matched.
_about.reach: A ROW DEFAULT REACHES ONLY RENDERED ROWS. The panel drops inert single-member rows and ladder rows that collapse to one choice, so parts living in those are still DEFAULT_PARTS_OFF / DEFAULT_PARTS_ON's business in render/monster.js. Those tables also feed stateParts() and the test that decides whether the Enraged checkbox appears at all, which nothing here can express.
_about.order: Dropdown order is the ROM's own member order unless a row carries an explicit `order` array of option keys, which then leads and unlisted options follow in ROM position. It has to be an ARRAY: the `options` object cannot carry order, because JS iterates integer-like keys ascending, so {"9":..,"1":..} comes back 1 then 9. Used where the ROM's order puts the damaged state above the healthy one -- Rathian's eye row reads 'Closed / Open' without it.
_about.rage: A monster entry may carry a `rage` map naming the Rage dropdown's rungs, keyed by that select's own value: 0 is No Rage, 1..n the rungs in order. rageLadder() otherwise reads them off the clip names, which gives 'Level 1' / 'Max' -- true to the ROM and meaningless to a player. Anything unnamed keeps the generated label.
_about.names: A `name` or an `options` entry means A PERSON TYPED IT while looking at the render -- that is what the row tooltip says, and what suppresses the community join's low/ambiguous/shared flags. So a MIGRATION from DEFAULT_PARTS_ON / DEFAULT_PARTS_OFF carries `default` ONLY: the default was already Raven's call, the names were not. Until he names them the row keeps its community name and its flags, which is the honest state.
_about.mergedRows: A row key joining several row keys with '+' replaces those rows with ONE control, and each of its options names one member per source row, joined the same way: "8,9+10,11": {options: {"8+10":"Intact", "9+10":"Cracked", "9+11":"Broken"}}. Both source clusters are still applied, one member each, exactly as two separate rows would -- this is presentation and nothing else. Refused, with a warning, if a source is a rage-ladder row: there the members are variants the Rage control picks between, and merging would take that decision away from it.
_about.reviewedRowsAlwaysShow: Naming a row makes the panel SHOW it, and makes the parts in its option keys the user's choice rather than the Rage control's. The panel normally folds away a cluster whose members differ only in what rage decides -- right for a rage aura, wrong for Tigrex's right front leg, where ROM_RAGE_SET happens to name parts 8 and 10 that are really a break state. This does not overrule the ROM about what rage DOES; the rage sets still apply. It changes only whether the row is offered.
_about.perStateOptionKeys: An option key written 'calmKey|rageKey' is ONE item with two forms: it resolves to whichever half the current state wants, and the other half is removed from the list so it is not offered as a third choice. Akantor's back row is the case -- 7, 8 and 8,9 are two states not three, 8 being the broken back and 8,9 the same break plus part 9, the layer its enraged form adds. Distinct from the row-level `rage` key, which chooses a different DEFAULT: here the choice does not move, only what it draws.
_about.rowOrder: A monster entry may carry a `rowOrder` array of row keys, which sets the order the Parts panel lists them in; anything it does not name keeps its cluster position after the ones it does. The panel otherwise follows the ROM's cluster order -- the order the parts table happens to be authored in, which put Ukanlos' eyes at the bottom under its tail.
_about.hiddenRows: A row may carry "hidden": true. Its default -- and its per-state `rage` default -- still apply, exactly as a visible row's would; it is simply not offered in the panel. For a consequence of the rage state rather than a choice anyone makes, like Gypceros' enraged eye glow.

em032_00.note: Reviewed by Raven 2026-09-10, including 'Right Front Leg (Missing currently)' -- and he was right, the row was not being drawn. Parts 8 and 10 are the right front leg, intact at 57v and broken at 15v, at x5-6; parts 7 and 9 are the left, 76v and 16v at x93-94. Two mirror images to within a few vertices, and only one had a control. The cause: ROM_RAGE_SET decodes em032_00 as [[1,0],[10,9]], so romRageParts() returns 8 and 10 as enrage parts, both members of the 8,10 cluster strip to nothing, the cluster folds to a single choice and the row is dropped as effect-only geometry. Naming the row now keeps it, and its option keys claim parts 8 and 10 back as the user's choice. The ROM is not overruled about what rage does -- its sets still apply -- and DEFAULT_PARTS_ON already had part 8 on in BOTH of Tigrex's states, so the entanglement was decided against before. THE EYES ROW IS THE ODD ONE: parts 1 and 2 are BOTH XfB__m02_eye, 22v each at the same point, and they are the calm and enraged eye -- which is why the Open item is keyed 'none'. Nothing of this row's own draws in that state; the eye that shows is picked by the Rage control from parts 1 and 2. Part 3 is the 16v body patch, so Closed. em032_00 KEEPS its DEFAULT_PARTS_ON {calm, rage} entry: it feeds stateParts() and the test that decides whether the Enraged control appears at all, neither of which a row default can reach.

em032_04.note: Reviewed by Raven 2026-09-10: 'Grimclaw should follow the same pattern as Tigrex'. It does, row for row, and NEEDED NO CODE FIX -- the earlier note that it was 'the same shape and still broken' was wrong. Every row was already drawn; only the names were off. THE 'MISSING LEG' WAS A MISLABEL, not a missing row. partnames.json calls row 7,9 'Back', so the panel read Head / Head / Back / Front Legs / Tail -- which looks like one back and ONE leg. Row 7,9 sits at x93 y66 z57 and row 8,10 at x6 y68 z55: mirror images, both at leg height and depth, and both within 2% of where Tigrex's legs sit. Two legs, correctly named now. AND NO BACK BREAK, checked rather than assumed -- Raven raised one and then withdrew it, noting 'sometimes the Deviants add part breaks'. Here this one did not. Grimclaw's 16 parts are Tigrex's 13 plus exactly five: 20 (m51_blood + m52_blood2), 30 (m61_angry_blood), 31 (m60_angry_arm), and the 6v decals 28 (m51_blood) and 38 (m61_angry_blood). Every one is a calm-or-enraged LAYER by material name, they sit in the one hidden cluster g0{0+ 20+ 30- 31- 100+} / g1{0+ 20- 30+ 31+ 100+} which is a calm/rage swap rather than a break, and no part of the model is absent from the visibility table (checked: every mesh's part id appears in a group). Worth re-running that check on each Deviant. WHERE IT DIFFERS FROM TIGREX, both harmless: (1) no part 2, so the Eyes row is 1,3 rather than 1,2,3 and its Open item is keyed 1 rather than 'none' -- Grimclaw has no separate enraged eye, and its g2 and g3 are byte-identical {1+ 3-}, folded to one option. (2) the right leg row carries parts 28 and 38, the calm and enraged blood decals; they are state parts, so the row already folded to 8 | 10 on its own and the Rage control still picks which decal rides along. em032_04 KEEPS its DEFAULT_PARTS_ON {calm, rage} entry -- it names 0, 20, 30, 31 and 100, and feeds stateParts().
